sections.content: How many people stayed in Filton after gaining qualifications?

Filton is a medium-sized town in the South West. Filton also has a university.

Filton has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Filton ended up with:

  • more graduates than it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 2,515 state-school pupils from Filton who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 775 (31%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 830 (33%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Filton to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Filton's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Filton in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Filton move to?

Of Filton's graduates, 290 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 105 of those graduates (36%) were living fairly locally, in the Bristol travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Filton's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 220 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 135 of those qualified non-graduates (61%) were living fairly locally, in the Bristol travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Filton's GCSE cohort:

  • 150 graduates left the South West
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 50 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the South West

In 2018 to 2019, 62% of graduates and 41% of qualified non-graduates living in Filton had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 1,260 graduates and 1,010 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Filton. This is compared with the 775 graduates and 830 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 38% of the graduates had also lived in Filton as GCSE pupils, while 62% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Filton in 2018 to 2019, 59% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 41% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
